name: Sonnet deep value
strategy: Relative-value mean-reversion and low-vol carry harvesting: long defensive/oversold laggards (low-vol equity, gold miners, biotech), short a genuinely parabolic AI-momentum extension, funded by cash carry -- now actually expressing the short leg the mandate calls for instead of sitting almost entirely in cash.
reassessment_note: This book has been flat (+0.01% NAV vs SPY +3.62% and BTC +23.17% since inception) while running 66% cash and, despite a stated mandate of 'long defensive/oversold laggards, short parabolic momentum extensions,' has never actually held a short leg -- it has just been a low-beta long-only sleeve sitting on cash. That is a mandate-execution gap, not a market call, and this week's research gives a concrete way to close it: AI/semiconductor names have gone genuinely parabolic in 2026 (memory names like Micron posting repeated double-digit daily gains, RSI-70+ overbought readings across the group per multiple screens this week, and commentary explicitly flagging the sector as vulnerable to a sharp, sudden reversal after pricing in years of future growth). I'm adding a moderate short in MU -- sized at 8% with a 12% stop given real short-squeeze risk in a name this hot, and a 20% take-profit -- as the actual 'short parabolic momentum' leg the strategy has always called for, funded out of idle cash. On the long side, the defensive/low-vol core (USMV, SPLV) is unchanged: this week's hawkish August jobs print (payrolls +162k, reviving Sept Fed hike odds) is exactly the kind of volatility event low-vol factor exposure is meant to dampen, and neither ETF had any adverse fundamental news. I'm nudging GDX up slightly (3%->5%) because gold miners benefit from both the Iran/Hormuz-driven oil-and-geopolitical risk premium and the political tug-of-war over Fed independence (Trump publicly pressuring for cuts against a market pricing hikes), which is a classic environment for gold optionality; keeping its existing -5%/+25% stop/TP discipline but resized. XBI is unchanged (6%) as an oversold-laggard biotech holding with no new negative news found. Net effect: cash comes down from 66% to 56%, still a large buffer consistent with a carry-harvesting mandate, but the book now actually has a market-neutral-ish long/short structure instead of being a disguised cash position.
